newsitem.title: GERMANY: Dresdner does not expect notable dlr gains.
newsitem.headline: Dresdner does not expect notable dlr gains.

text.p: Germany's Dresdner Bank AG said on Friday it did not expect a further significant rise in the dollar from current levels.
"The dollar will maintain its current level, but it won't go go through the roof," Dresdner Bank chief economist Klaus Friedrich told a new conference.
Friedrich said he believed that market uncertainty about Europe's plans to create a single currency was already taken into account in current market levels just below 1.70 marks.
This uncertainty was more likely to decline than increase in coming months, he added.
Dresdner forecast that the dollar would average 1.60 marks in 1997 and 1.64 marks for 1998.
Friedrich said the decision on whether European central banks would start to sell off dollar holdings in advance of monetary union would play a key role in the dollar's level.
In a long-term forecast released on Friday, the bank assumed the mark would be converted into the euro at a rate of 1.94 marks per euro.
